verdict.rationale: Muse lets users name the agent, give it a unique style, and "shape how it talks" (muse-docs-17, muse-docs-2), which implies persistent persona or tone customization. Users can also inspect and edit Muse's memory about them and use a Forget skill to prune it (muse-supp-vm-files-export, muse-docs-12). That memory editing serves as an indirect way to set persistent preferences, but no dedicated custom-instructions feature is documented. Missing for 10: an explicit custom-instructions or preferences setting, documentation that these settings apply to every response, depth on what can be configured beyond style, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
